caseno: Appeal From Original Decree No. 200 of 1996
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim with Mr. Ali Imam Khaled Rahim, Advocates ----- for the defendant-appellants. 
Mr. A.B. Mahfuzur Rahman with Mr. Md. Elahi Bakhsh, Advocates ----- for Respondents.
parties:
Md Monir Hossain and others
Vs.
Md Shamsul Hoque Mondal and others
full_judgment:
Md. Abdus Salam, J: This appeal at the instance of defendant-appellants is directed against the impugned judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenidah in Title Suit No. 75 of 1994 mainly on the grounds, among others, that in view of the fact and finding of the Subordinate Judge that the power of attorney in question does not contain the counter signature of the Deputy High Commissioner of Pakistan in Calcutta, the said power of attorney allegedly executed by Shyamapada and others in favour of Shahid Dhabak and Ahar Ali is of doubtful origin; that the Subordinate Judge committed error of law by placing the onus of proving the genuineness and regularity of the auction sale upon the defendant' in utter disregard of the provisions of section 114(E) of the Evidence Act which provides for presumption of regularity and legality of all official acts; that the Court below erred in law in not holding that the auction purchaser purchased the suit property before the alleged exchange and took delivery of possession through Court which is proved by the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession; that the Subordinate Judge illegally embarked upon an investigation as to the possession of each plot of land without considering that the writ of delivery of possession followed the kabala deed of the defendant and sufficiently proves possession of the plaintiff in the suit land; that Shaheed Dhabak and Ahar Ali did not come forward before that Court to support the case of the plaintiff in view of the alleged exchange of the suit property and the Court below committed error of law in relying upon the false and concocted story of the plaintiffs that the heirs of Shaheed Dhabak possessed plot Nos. 1209, 668, 669, 677, 678, 678, 655 and 682 as their homestead and that after the death of Ahar Ali his heirs plaintiff Nos. 2-6 have been possessing the khaw schedule land through borgader, even though no borgader came forward to depose in support of this claim and that the Subordinate Judge illegally held that the order dated 25.3.1981 passed by Revenue Authority in Miscellaneous Case No.165/IP/69/70 is not binding upon the plaintiff though the competent authority found upon enquiry that the alleged exchange of the plaintiff and the disputed power of attorney are fake and forged. 

 10. On a careful scrutiny of the documentary and oral evidence on record we find nothing to differ from the finding and observation of the trial Court about the genuineness of the disputed power of attorney Ext. 1(A) and exchange of the suit property. Moreover, according to the principles laid down in the case law reported in 10 D.L.R. page 1, Privy Council, K.M. Perera Vs. H.G. Martin Dias with the observation of Lord Denning and the case law reported in 36 D.L.R.(AD) Page 52 Md. Badruddin Khan Vs. Bangladesh and others in which the Appellate Division of Bangladesh Supreme Court observed that trial Court's findings should not be easily disturbed as a matter of course and before reversing the findings and decisions of the trial Court, the Appellate Court should think twice or more than twice. We do not find any error of law or of facts in the impugned judgment and decree delivered by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd court, Jhenidah. Moreover, in a Civil Matter, all the facts alleged by plaintiff. need not be proved strictly in view of the decision in the case of Jahed Ali Mondal Vs. Jamini Kanta Dey reported in 7 BLD(AD)page 156 and the burden of proof is lightened by presumption, admission and estoppel in view of this case law. It appears that the plaintiffs-respondents have discharged their primary onus to prove the genuineness of the disputed power of attorney Ext. 1(A). The six Govt. rent receipts Ext. 1 (d) upto 1(i) show that the kabala deed dated 13.2.64 executed by Samapada Biswas in favour of Santosh Kumar has been acted upon and the defendant appellants did not take any step for proving possession of the contesting defendants by producing any Govt. rent receipts along with the documentary evidence from Ext. 'A' upto Ext. (J).
